name: @aztec-avm-runtime/orchestration
description: Aztec's own public transaction orchestration, over the wasm AVM
//: WHAT IS AND IS NOT IN THIS PACKAGE, corrected in M18's review because the first version of
this note said the opposite. The three-phase transaction model, the state manager, the block
processor, the side-effect trace, the DB interfaces and the public DB sources are NOT
vendored here. REUSE-INVENTORY RI-19..RI-23 record the DECISION to vendor them; the files
are not under src/ and @aztec/simulator is not a dependency, because upstream does not
publish it. What this package is today is the SEAM and its two encoders — a simulator over
the wasm AVM, the copied checkpoint, the telemetry replacement and the named configurations.
Running a transaction through upstream's own PublicProcessor still needs RI-19..RI-23 to be
carried out; see M18's outstanding tasks.
WHAT IS HERE IS UPSTREAM'S. The msgpack encoder for the AVM's own input schema is — it is
`serializeWithMessagePack` in @aztec/stdlib/avm, which is what CppPublicTxSimulator calls
on exactly this type. What is ours is the transport: where CppPublicTxSimulator hands the
encoded blob to @aztec/native's `avmSimulate`, WasmAvmPublicTxSimulator hands it to
avm.wasm through @aztec-avm-runtime/node-host.
@aztec/telemetry-client is DELIBERATELY ABSENT from the dependency list. It is replaced
by src/telemetry.ts, and the reason is measured rather than assumed: see that file.
@aztec/native and @aztec/world-state are DELIBERATELY ABSENT too. The first is the C++
AVM over NAPI, which DD-9 says no public export of ours may reach; the second is an
LMDB-backed native addon, replaced by Aztec's own world_state_reference compiled into
avm.wasm (RI-27). ForkCheckpoint, the one production import that package supplied to this
subtree, is copied into src/fork_checkpoint.ts.
